title: United States Grain Standards Reauthorization Act of 2020
official_summary:
United States Grain Standards Reauthorization Act of 2020

This bill reauthorizes through FY2025 the United States Grain Standards Act, which authorizes the Department of Agriculture (USDA) to establish official marketing standards for grains, and to provide procedures for grain inspection and weighing.

Additionally, the bill

  • requires a state agency to notify customers or applicants for weighing or inspection services if it intends to temporarily discontinue the services;
  • extends the authority of USDA to collect fees to fund official inspections and provide official weighing services through FY2025;
  • extends the cap on the administrative and supervisory costs through FY2025;
  • requires USDA to publish quarterly reports describing data from the tests and inspections for intrinsic quality factors (including protein, oil, and starch) and food safety factors;
  • requires USDA to publish quarterly reports including the number of certain waivers and exceptions that were requested and granted;
  • prohibits the use of user fees for activities related to the development or maintenance of grain standards, or for any activity that is not directly related to the performance of an official inspection or weighing service;
  • provides that members of the advisory committee with respect to the act may serve up to two consecutive terms and extends the authorization of the committee through FY2025; and
  • requires USDA to conduct a comprehensive nationwide review of the official agency geographical areas.

summary.headline: A 2020 law extends USDA's authority over grain inspection, weighing, and grading through fiscal year 2025 and adds reporting and review requirements.
summary.what_it_does: The law reauthorizes the United States Grain Standards Act through fiscal year 2025, which lets USDA set official grain marketing standards and set rules for grain inspection and weighing. It extends USDA's power to collect fees that pay for official inspections and weighing, and it keeps the cap on administrative and supervisory costs in place through the same year. It also requires quarterly USDA reports on grain quality and food safety test data and on certain waivers and exceptions, bars user fees from paying for work not directly tied to inspections or weighing, lets advisory committee members serve up to two consecutive terms, and requires a nationwide review of official agency geographic areas.

who_it_affects.how: They are affected by the continued federal grain standards and inspection system that sets how their grain is graded and weighed.

who_it_affects.group: Grain elevators, exporters, and other businesses that pay for official inspection and weighing
who_it_affects.how: They continue to pay USDA-authorized fees for these services, and those fees may not be used for activities outside official inspection or weighing.

who_it_affects.group: State agencies that provide grain inspection or weighing services
who_it_affects.how: They must notify customers or applicants before temporarily stopping these services.

who_it_affects.group: Customers and applicants for official grain weighing or inspection
who_it_affects.how: They receive advance notice if a state agency plans to temporarily stop providing these services.

who_it_affects.group: Members of the grain standards advisory committee
who_it_affects.how: They may serve up to two consecutive terms, and the committee's authorization is extended through fiscal year 2025.

who_it_affects.group: Official inspection agencies operating in designated geographic areas
who_it_affects.how: Their service areas will be reviewed nationwide by USDA.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: Enacted December 11, 2020, with the reauthorization running through fiscal year 2025.
